title: Krasner neighbourhoods over henselian fields of arbitrary valuation rank
statement: Let $F$ be a field with a nontrivial valuation and henselian valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Let $N/F$ be a finite Galois extension: finite, separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and normal, meaning that every minimal polynomial of an element of $N$ over $F$ splits in $N[T]$. Fix a valuation $w$ of $N$ prolonging that of $F$, with values in a totally ordered abelian group, written additively. For $\alpha,\beta\in N$, suppose that $w(\alpha-\beta)>w(\alpha-\sigma(\alpha))$ for every $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}_F(N)$ with $\sigma(\alpha)\ne\alpha$. Then $\alpha\in F(\beta)$, where $F(\beta)$ is the smallest subfield containing $F$ and $\beta$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Thus there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $\alpha$ in $N$ such that every $\beta\in U$ satisfies $\alpha\in F(\beta)$. When $\alpha\in F$ the condition is empty and one may take $U=N$. No completeness or rank restriction is imposed. Here an additive valuation has $w(0)=\infty$, $w(x)\in\Gamma$ for $x\ne0$, $w(xy)=w(x)+w(y)$ and $w(x+y)\geq\min\{w(x),w(y)\}$; its topology has the balls $\{x:w(x-a)>\gamma\}$, $a\in N$, $\gamma\in\Gamma$, as a basis. Its valuation ring is $\mathcal O_w=\{x:w(x)\geq0\}$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, forms of Krasner lemma, reference to Bourbaki, Algebre commutative VI section 8 exercises 12 and 14(a). Stacks Tag 09EI only treats a complete one-dimensional local domain, and is not a source for the unrestricted-rank statement.

proof.text: Put $G=\operatorname{Aut}_F(N)$ and $\mathcal O=\{x\in N:w(x)\geq0\}$. For $\sigma\in G$, $w\circ\sigma$ is another prolongation of the valuation on $F$, since $\sigma$ fixes $F$. By [lem-per-henselian-finite-extension-topology], applied to the finite algebraic extension $N/F$, the two prolongations have the same valuation subring. Consequently $\sigma^{-1}(\mathcal O)=\mathcal O$. Only uniqueness of the prolongation up to equality of valuation subrings is used; none of the topology-comparison clauses is used.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374: forms of Krasner lemma; explicit agent-written finite-Galois argument

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field], $G$ is finite. Thus each $\sigma\in G$ has finite order: two powers agree in the finite list of powers, and cancellation gives $\sigma^n=1$ for some $n>0$. For nonzero $a,b\in N$, $w(a)\geq w(b)$ is equivalent to $a/b\in\mathcal O$. Step 1 and $\sigma(a/b)=\sigma(a)/\sigma(b)$ therefore give $w(\sigma a)\geq w(\sigma b)$ if and only if $w(a)\geq w(b)$, and likewise preserve strict comparisons. If $w(\sigma x)>w(x)$ for nonzero $x$, iterating this comparison gives $w(x)<w(\sigma x)<\cdots<w(\sigma^n x)=w(x)$, a contradiction; the reversed strict inequality gives the reversed contradiction. Totality now gives $w(\sigma x)=w(x)$. This holds for $x=0$ as well, since $\sigma0=0$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374: forms of Krasner lemma; explicit agent-written finite-Galois argument

proof.text: Let $\beta$ satisfy the stated inequalities. Take any $\sigma\in G$ fixing $\beta$. If $\sigma\alpha\ne\alpha$, put $d=\alpha-\beta$. Step 2 gives $w(\sigma\alpha-\beta)=w(\sigma d)=w(d)$. The valuation inequality applied to $\alpha-\sigma\alpha=d-\sigma d$ yields $w(\alpha-\sigma\alpha)\geq\min\{w(d),w(\sigma d)\}=w(\alpha-\beta)$, contradicting the strict hypothesis for this $\sigma$. Hence every automorphism in $G$ fixing $\beta$ fixes $\alpha$. This also covers $d=0$, when the same inequality has right side $\infty$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374: forms of Krasner lemma; explicit agent-written finite-Galois argument

proof.text: Let $L=F(\beta)\subseteq N$. An $F$-automorphism of $N$ fixes $\beta$ if and only if it fixes $L$ pointwise: the elements it fixes form a subfield containing $F$ and $\beta$, and $L$ is the smallest such subfield. The extension $N/F$ is Galois by hypothesis, so [lem-exc-etale-galois-fixed-field-subgroup] identifies the fixed field of this fixing subgroup with $L$. Step 3 says that $\alpha$ belongs to that fixed field. Thus $\alpha\in F(\beta)$.

source.place: InfiniteGalois.fixedField_fixingSubgroup, line 85; elementary description of the subgroup fixing a generated field

proof.text: For the neighbourhood clause, let $S=\{\sigma\in G:\sigma\alpha\ne\alpha\}$. It is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field]. If $S$ is nonempty, the finite nonempty subset $\{w(\alpha-\sigma\alpha):\sigma\in S\}$ of the totally ordered value group has a largest element $r$ (take successive larger values). Set $U=\{\beta\in N:w(\alpha-\beta)>r\}$. This is a basic open ball and contains $\alpha$, since $w(0)=\infty>r$. Each $\beta\in U$ satisfies every required strict inequality, so Step 4 applies. If $S$ is empty, $\alpha$ is fixed by all of $G$, hence $\alpha\in F$ by the fixed-field clause of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field]; take $U=N$, since $F\subseteq F(\beta)$ for all $\beta$. In particular this is the specified choice when $\alpha\in F$. Only a finite maximum is taken; there is no completeness or rank assumption.

Step 5: a finite maximum r is taken in the value group and the ball around α is a basic open set. If S is empty, IsGalois.mem_range_algebraMap_iff_fixed (Basic.lean:340, read) gives α∈F and U=N.
